en: The Apadāna of the Elder Saraṇagamaniya Saddasaññaka Chapter 9 I was a merchant in the city of Benares, and I possessed great wealth. At that time, the Buddha, the Blessed One, had arrived at Benares. Having heard of his arrival, I went to the Teacher. There, I saw the Teacher, the Blessed One, the Tathāgata, the Arhat, the Perfectly Enlightened One, who was seated amidst a circle of monks. Having seen him, I approached the Teacher and paid homage at his feet. Then, having circumambulated him three times, I sat down to one side. As I sat there, the Teacher, the Blessed One, taught me the Dhamma with its many aspects. Having heard that Dhamma, I attained the fruit of stream-entry. Then, taking up my bowl and robe, I departed from the presence of the Teacher. I went to my own home and addressed my wife: "My dear, I have become a stream-enterer; I shall go forth into homelessness. She replied: "Noble sir, do not go forth; remain here for a long time. A second time and a third time I spoke thus, and a second and a third time she replied: "Noble sir, do not go forth; remain here for a long time. When she would not permit it, I took her by the hand and led her out of the house. Having gone outside, I said to her: "My dear, I am going forth into homelessness; you may stay here or come along. She replied: "Noble sir, I will come along. Taking both our bowls and robes, we went to the Teacher. Having approached him, we paid homage at his feet and stood to one side. Standing there, I requested of the Teacher: "May the Blessed One grant us the going-forth; may the Blessed One ordain us. Then the Teacher, the Blessed One, granted us the going-forth and ordained us. Having been ordained, we applied ourselves to meditation. Through diligent application, we both realized the state of Arahantship. We then addressed the Teacher: "Blessed One, we wish to go to our own village to see our parents. The Teacher consented by remaining silent. Having received his permission, we took our bowls and robes and set out for our own village. On the way, we saw a certain man who was suffering from a severe illness. Seeing him, we asked: "Sir, what is your ailment? He replied: "Venerable sirs, I am afflicted by a severe illness. We then asked: "Sir, do you have any relatives? He replied: "Venerable sirs, I have no relatives. We then asked: "Sir, where do you wish to go? He replied: "Venerable sirs, I wish to go to the world of the gods. We then said to him: "Sir, if you wish to go to the world of the gods, take refuge in the Buddha, take refuge in the Dhamma, and take refuge in the Saṅgha.

Having spoken thus, we continued on our way. Upon reaching our own village, we went to our parents' house. Having approached them, we paid homage at their feet and sat down to one side. As we sat there, we informed our parents: "Father, Mother, we have become Arahants. Hearing this, they were filled with joy and said: "Dear sons, since you have become Arahants, you may enjoy the bliss of the Dhamma. We then reflected: "If we were to enjoy the bliss of the Dhamma while staying here, our parents would constantly worry about us. It would be better for us to dwell in the forest. Reflecting thus, we took our bowls and robes and departed for the forest. There, we dwelt in a secluded place, enjoying the bliss of the Dhamma. Later, when we returned to our parents' house, we paid homage at their feet and sat down to one side. As we sat there, we informed them: "Father, Mother, we have dwelt in the forest and enjoyed the bliss of the Dhamma. Hearing this, they were filled with even greater joy and said: "Dear sons, since you have dwelt in the forest and enjoyed the bliss of the Dhamma, you may continue to enjoy that bliss. Thus did we, through the power of the Triple Gem, attain the supreme goal. This is the Apadāna of the Elder Saraṇagamaniya.
